newsitem.title: JAPAN: Earthquake in southern Japan injures four.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake in southern Japan injures four.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale shook Japan's southern island of Kyushu on Thursday, injuring at least four people and causing landslides in the region.

The tremor struck Kagoshima Prefecture on Kyushu island at 4.33 a.m. on Thursday (1933 GMT on Wednesday), with the epicentre near the city of Kagoshima, 800 km (500 miles) southwest of Tokyo, the Meteorological Agency said.
A Kagoshima police spokesman said the earthquake caused minor injuries to four people, including a nine-year-old boy hit by falling furniture.
The tremor, combined with heavy rain the previous night, set off small landslides at 14 locations, forcing about 30 residents to evacuate their homes.
There was minor damage to several main roads and trains were temporarily halted until inspection crews declared there was no damage to railway lines.
The Meteorological Agency said Thursday's tremor was the largest aftershock so far from an earthquake that struck the same area on March 26.
The March 26 earthquake measured 6.2 on the Richter scale and injured 20 people.
